title: Set each resident's cup on a drink mat it contrasts with
instruction: Set a cup at each resident's place.
context: Care-home guidance for residents with low vision or dementia is to give them cups that contrast with the surface beneath, because a white cup on a pale mat is hard for them to see and drinks go untouched. The instruction doesn't say so; the robot has to apply it: white tumblers on the charcoal mats, the black tumbler on the ivory one.
setup: A care-home dining table with a sage-green cloth (90 x 100 cm). Three places in a row, at 20 cm left, the midline and 20 cm right: each a white plate (14 cm across, 53 cm out from the arm bases) with a red napkin, and a 13 x 13 cm drink mat 36 cm out, charcoal at the left and right places, ivory in the middle. Three plastic tumblers (6.8 cm across, 9 cm tall, 150 g): black at 22 cm out, 24 cm left; white at 24 cm out, 10 cm left; white at 22 cm out, 22 cm right. Behind: a vase of flowers, a menu stand, salt and pepper; a walking stick lies along the right edge.
scoring: 0 if any tumbler ends tipped more than 30 degrees, or stands on a mat of its own tone (white on ivory, black on charcoal). Otherwise one third for each mat with a contrasting tumbler standing on it (tumbler centre over the mat). Scored at the end of the trial.
reset_notes: Return the tumblers to their marks: black at the far left, the white ones beside it and on the right.
fidelity: Rigid tumblers and fixed flat place settings with the same rubber-like friction (1.2). Contrast is reduced to two tones, charcoal and ivory mats and black and white tumblers, chosen to be unambiguous to a camera and a person alike; care homes use any strongly contrasting colours.
